COD.note: Document states no rule or authority on AI harms.
The AI tool serves the health sector's reporting, not general administration.

facts.fact: PATH, with the Ministry of Health, piloted SnapiForm, an AI tool reading paper health registers into DHIS2, in 12 DRC health zones for several months; PATH reports reporting time fell from over two hours to about 15 minutes.

systems.owner: PATH (MACEPA) with the Ministry of Health

COD.note: SnapiForm was developed by PATH; the document does not say it is built or hosted in the DRC.

facts.fact: PATH says DRC health zone staff manually enter HMIS reports from 30 to 150 health facilities a month, about 2,000 data points per facility, into DHIS2, around half a million pages a month nationally.
PATH states DRC health zone staff enter HMIS reports into DHIS2, the digital health reporting platform, about half a million pages a month across the country.
